raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Keep positioned prefixes useful under CPU-offload LRU pressure while their request is still running, across store batches and KV groups. Related to [this observation in #58804](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58804#issuecomment-6098736505); this does not claim to explain or resolve all throughput regression in that issue.

## Claims

- Newly observed and inserted keys share one provisional request rank, with later token positions evicted first across batches.
- Existing-prefix reuse, transfer pinning, newer shared accesses, and cache resets retain their ordering contracts.
- No repeated full-prefix refresh; ARC frequency accounting stays at finalization and external policies inherit a no-op hook.

## Validation

Python base: `187a0eb98aa42341d703f83421d693fa7585581b`, Linux x86_64, Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Added tests against the base manager/LRU | 11 failed, 2 passed |
| CPU manager and policy factory | 72 passed |
| Tiering and offloading scheduler | 465 passed |
| Complete cloud rerun on 2026-10-11 | 537 passed |
| All applicable pre-commit hooks, including mypy | Passed |

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/test_factory.py
PYTHONPATH=/workspace/vllm-onboarding/offload-prefix-repro HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p offline_model -q tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/base.py vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/lru.py vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/manager.py tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py
```

The cloud-only `offline_model` fixture plugin supplies a local OPT configuration in place of the test factory's default `facebook/opt-125m` model parameter because model-host access was blocked. All other configuration parameters, production code and assertions remained active; no OPT weights were used. The unmodified base fails the same representative online-config tests before test setup under this network restriction. In a network-enabled checkout, omit the plugin and offline environment settings to use the ordinary test fixture.

Native CPU inference: two-layer tiny Llama with dummy weights, float32, greedy decoding, two 192-token prompts, block size 32, eight offload slots. A remains generating while B fills the tier. After aborting A and clearing only the model-side prefix cache, replay A:

| Metric | Base manager/LRU | This change |
|---|---:|---:|
| Second-turn cached tokens | 0 | 64 |
| Real KV pages read back | 0 | 2 |
| Output token IDs | 21, 17, 21, 17 | 21, 17, 21, 17 |

This executes the native CPU model using a test-only out-of-tree worker that copies real CPU KV pages synchronously. Existing CPU native extensions built at `e5d33a36e` were reused for both runs; only the manager/LRU differs. The separate real scheduler replay with three groups changes retained A positions from `[4,5]` to `[0,1]` in each group and issues a two-block load per group on the second turn.

CUDA transfer behavior, GPU TTFT/throughput, FS tiering and the reporter's Qwen/DFlash workload have not been measured. The dummy model checks usable KV reuse and the observed output, not model quality.

## Details

Insertion ranks previously left an unfinished request's head older than its tail until finalization. A later request could evict the head, making every remaining suffix chunk unreachable by contiguous-prefix lookup.

The new hook distinguishes fresh allocation from first observation. LRU assigns positioned keys `(request_rank, -token_position)` during the request, including already resident keys it reuses. The provisional rank is anchored at first observation, finalization still commits recency, and older requests cannot demote a newer shared access. Reset invalidates provisional state. Keys without token positions retain insertion ordering; chunks remain evictable rather than pinned.

The existing heap update/compaction path is reused. This adds a tuple per cached rank and a small scratch state per request, and has measurable bookkeeping cost:

<details>
<summary>CPU manager microbenchmark and variability</summary>


| Chunks/group (9 groups, batches of 8) | Base default median [min,max], ms | Changed default median [min,max], ms | Base full-prefix refresh median, ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 | 1.40 [1.31,2.10] | 1.79 [1.68,2.37] | 2.68 |
| 256 | 6.19 [5.94,9.04] | 7.75 [7.55,10.01] | 24.99 |
| 1024 | 26.75 [24.82,298.47] | 34.34 [34.05,309.39] | 414.57 |

Five runs per case, timing manager stores and position recording only. Median overhead is approximately 25–28% compared with the incorrect base ordering, but avoids the full-refresh alternative's repeated traversal (594,432 additional touch-key visits in the largest case). These CPU microbenchmarks do not establish a serving speedup. A regression test bounds token-position queries linearly without a timing threshold.

</details>

Not a duplicate: #57813 adds optional in-flight pin preference and saturation fallback across policies; #50422 adds SAE; #57746 records GPU-local reuse; #60469 changes KVCR recency. None fixes this default LRU cross-batch order. Checked issue comments and open PR searches for `58804 in:body`, offload LRU/prefix/session/recency and LRU tail.

AI assistance from OpenAI Codex was used during development.

🚀

Thanks for picking this up. I ran it on the Qwen/DFlash workload from my #58804 comment, which the description lists as unmeasured: it brings back the second-turn reuse that 0.31.0 loses there, with no chunk 0 evicted.

Setup: a native RTX 3090, Qwen3.8-27B W4A16 (GDN + attention, DFlash drafter, 9 KV-cache groups), vLLM 0.31.0 with an out-of-tree patch series (on the offload path it only adds a boot-time warning and a device-pointer translation that adds 0 on native Linux), `--kv-offloading-size 8`, two ~60K-token conversations in flight at once, then each conversation's second turn. The PR cherry-picks onto 0.31.0 without conflicts (the series leaves those three files as upstream ships them). One boot per row:

| | turn 2 cached | read back from CPU |
|---|---|---|
| 0.30.0 | 57,664 and 57,664 (96.3%) | 2.16 GB |
| 0.31.0 | 0 and 0 | 0 |
| 0.31.0 + this PR | 50,880 of 59,718 (85.2%) and 49,184 of 59,887 (82.1%) | 1.90 GB |

With the PR the tier evicts 120 chunks, tail-first within each request, none of them a chunk 0; on 0.31.0 the first victims are chunk 0 of all nine groups.

I had also tried re-ranking a running request's whole observed prefix after each of its store batches. On this workload that gives the same counts to the token and the same victims, so your cheaper bookkeeping costs nothing in hits here. This workload does not exercise the cross-request order, though: at each eviction burst only one request had evictable chunks, so the shared provisional rank had nothing to choose between. That reading comes from the victim list, not from a run built to test it.

Unit, on the same 0.31.0 tree, CPU only: `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py` and `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies` give 73 passed with the PR, including a test of mine that stores a positioned four-chunk prefix in two batches and expects the tail to go first. Without the PR, those 12 fail (your 11 and mine).

Still unproven: one boot per row and one workload. The rest of the gap to 0.30.0 is tail chunks of every group, attention groups included; for a hybrid model a windowed group's chunks inside the hit would be better victims, but that needs each group's window, so it is a separate change.

This was measured and written with AI assistance (Claude); every number above comes from our own runs.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

+    """Keep a contiguous prefix while its owner is still generating."""
+    manager = make_cpu_manager(num_chunks=8)

+                ctx.set_offload_key_position(group[position], (position + 1) * 16)

+        batches.append(batch)

+            manager.complete_store(batch, ctx)

+        for batch in reversed(batches):
+            manager.complete_store(batch, ctx)
+
+    output = manager.prepare_store(to_keys([10, 11, 12, 13]), make_req_context("B"))
+    assert output is not None
+    assert set(output.evicted_keys) == {group[-1] for group in groups}

+

+
+def test_lru_failed_store_retry_preserves_prefix_order():

+

🚀

Thanks for picking this up. I ran it on the Qwen/DFlash workload from my #58804 comment, which the description lists as unmeasured: it brings back the second-turn reuse that 0.31.0 loses there, with no chunk 0 evicted.

Setup: a native RTX 3090, Qwen3.8-27B W4A16 (GDN + attention, DFlash drafter, 9 KV-cache groups), vLLM 0.31.0 with an out-of-tree patch series (on the offload path it only adds a boot-time warning and a device-pointer translation that adds 0 on native Linux), `--kv-offloading-size 8`, two ~60K-token conversations in flight at once, then each conversation's second turn. The PR cherry-picks onto 0.31.0 without conflicts (the series leaves those three files as upstream ships them). One boot per row:

| | turn 2 cached | read back from CPU |
|---|---|---|
| 0.30.0 | 57,664 and 57,664 (96.3%) | 2.16 GB |
| 0.31.0 | 0 and 0 | 0 |
| 0.31.0 + this PR | 50,880 of 59,718 (85.2%) and 49,184 of 59,887 (82.1%) | 1.90 GB |

With the PR the tier evicts 120 chunks, tail-first within each request, none of them a chunk 0; on 0.31.0 the first victims are chunk 0 of all nine groups.

I had also tried re-ranking a running request's whole observed prefix after each of its store batches. On this workload that gives the same counts to the token and the same victims, so your cheaper bookkeeping costs nothing in hits here. This workload does not exercise the cross-request order, though: at each eviction burst only one request had evictable chunks, so the shared provisional rank had nothing to choose between. That reading comes from the victim list, not from a run built to test it.

Unit, on the same 0.31.0 tree, CPU only: `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py` and `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies` give 73 passed with the PR, including a test of mine that stores a positioned four-chunk prefix in two batches and expects the tail to go first. Without the PR, those 12 fail (your 11 and mine).

Still unproven: one boot per row and one workload. The rest of the gap to 0.30.0 is tail chunks of every group, attention groups included; for a hybrid model a windowed group's chunks inside the hit would be better victims, but that needs each group's window, so it is a separate change.

This was measured and written with AI assistance (Claude); every number above comes from our own runs.
